label: mutually exclusive with
type: SYMMETRIC: subject and object cannot both be selected, enabled or in progress at the same time. Both slots are concepts of the same kind; the direction carries no meaning.
note: Round 26's most-used new predicate and the first genuinely SYMMETRIC one in the registry - every other relation here has a directed reading, and this one does not, which matters because a consumer that walks the graph in one direction only will miss half of these. Its four files split into two unrelated families: cluster authentication (Native LDAP versus saslauthd - 'The two cannot be used simultaneously') and Eventing (function lifecycle operations versus the Eventing rebalance operation, stated on both the Server and Capella copies of eventing-lifecycle). Two independent subject areas reaching for the same relation is the evidence that it is a schema-level primitive rather than a security detail. Distinct from mustUseInsteadWhen (a directed substitution rule) and from doesNotSupport (a capability absence, not a conflict between two present things).
relates_to_competency_question: Which pairs of features cannot be enabled at the same time?
